From: Claire Ramos <claire.ramos@borealtech.com>

Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated capacity increase + isolation request

Hi Neha,

We're coming up on our renewal with Redwood (end of July) and we'd like to discuss expanding our Dedicated capacity as part of the new term. Current ask from the platform team: provision an additional 24 A100-equivalent GPUs in a reserved pool, and ensure that the pool is logically isolated from other tenants (we need tenant separation for compliance).

Specific asks:
- Add +24 GPUs to our reserved capacity starting on renewal effective date (2026-07-31).
- Confirm exact isolation mechanism (logical fencing, tenant tagging, and network-level separation where possible).
- Throughput guarantees we can expect for our workload (we're running long-context chat + embed-heavy batch jobs; baseline steady-state throughput target is ~10k tokens/sec with predictable tail latencies).
- Any term/price changes if we move to an annual prepay vs month-to-month.

I've attached our latest utilization export for reference. Can we get a short proposal by EOD next week? We're coordinating procurement and security sign-off.

Thanks,
Claire Ramos
Head of Platform Operations
BorealTech

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: Dedicated capacity increase + isolation request

Thanks for the ping. Short answers:

1) Isolation approach (recommended):
- Logical fencing via tenant tags + scheduler-level allocation: we assign a dedicated node pool with reserved GPU instances that are tainted for BorealTech workloads only; Kubernetes scheduling rules + runtime enforcement prevent cross-tenant pods from landing on those nodes.
- Network controls: we isolate egress via dedicated subnets and optional private peering; control plane access remains logical (we can add IP allowlists for management endpoints).
- Audit & access: audit logs for node/user actions are retained for 13 months by default, can be extended. We can add a read-only audit view for customer SOC review under an NDA.

2) Throughput & SLOs (for +24 A100-equivalent GPUs):
- Steady-state throughput baseline: 10k tokens/sec sustained across the pool for mixed streaming + batch, with headroom for short bursts.
- Latency: P95 streaming response latency target under 4k context: <150ms for interactive models; embeddings batch latency depends on batch size but 95% within expected window if batched correctly.
- We can commit to a throughput target in the SOW (we typically model based on expected concurrency and tokens/sec).

3) Burst & billing:
- Burst capacity: we recommend a small shared burst bucket (10% of reserved capacity) that can temporarily absorb spikes. Beyond that, on-demand capacity will be billed at on-demand token pricing (or we can include pre-purchased burst credits).

Attached is a minimal pool config that maps to our internal deployment template. If legal requires explicit tenant separation language, we'll include the fencing mechanics in the SOW.

Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Platform Ops Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated capacity increase + isolation request — proposal and SOW

Hi Claire,

Thanks for the patience — we've reviewed internally and put together the attached SOW and proposed commercial terms. Summary below:

- Capacity: +24 A100-equivalent GPUs added to a reserved, tenant-fenced pool effective on renewal date (2026-07-31).
- Isolation: node-level fencing (taints/tolerations) + dedicated subnet and peering for network separation. Audit logs retained 13 months; we can add extended retention as a contract add-on.
- Throughput SLO: Baseline 10k tokens/sec sustained across the pool with P95 streaming latency <150ms on 4k contexts under normal load. We will include measurement hooks in Console dashboards and run an acceptance test during rollout.
- Burst: 10% burst bucket included; additional on-demand capacity billed at standard on-demand rates or covered via purchased burst credits.
- Term & pricing: Option A — annual prepay with 12% discount vs monthly; Option B — 12-month commit billed monthly. Pricing details and line items are in the attached SOW (SOW_v3.pdf).

Action items:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the technical bullets and preferred commercial option by 7/14 so procurement can start paperwork.
2) If accepted, we'll issue the SOW via DocuSign and schedule a brief acceptance test on rollout week (target 7/31 - 8/3).

Link to SOW (preview): https://docusign.com/link/SOW-78340

Thanks — copying Sean and Vivek for any final additions.

Best,
